title: Self-adjoint norm bound
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $T$ be an operator on real-valued functions on its outcome space. Suppose $T$ is self-adjoint with respect to product expectation, meaning $\mathbb E_P[(Tf)g]=\mathbb E_P[f(Tg)]$ for all functions $f,g$. If $q>1$, $A>0$, and $\|Tg\|_{q/(q-1),P}\le A\|g\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ for every $g$, then $\|Tf\|_{q,P}\le A\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$T$ is an operator on real-valued functions on the product outcome space
$T$ is self-adjoint with respect to product expectation
$T$ satisfies the stated norm bound at exponent $q/(q-1)$ for every function
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q>1$, $A>0$, and an operator $T$ on real functions on $\Omega$. If $\mathbb E_P[(Tf)g]=\mathbb E_P[fTg]$ for every $f,g$ and $\|Tg\|_{q/(q-1),P}\le A\|g\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ for every $g$, then $\|Tf\|_{q,P}\le A\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every $f$.
